auditor_pwc: Hi team — PwC here. We need SOC 2 evidence and a short repro for the auth-related incident on 2026-02-18. Specifically: 1) the retention policy for auth sessions/refresh tokens, 2) the sampling methodology and samples for auth logs, 3) reproducible steps (scripts/playbook) that replay the auth 401 -> client retry loop that preceded the billing spike. Prefer S3 links to exported bundles + a manifest.csv + SHA256s. ETA: EOD Thursday if possible.

ben-security: Got it. We'll assemble an evidence bundle. Quick clarifying Qs: do you need HSM-signed manifests or is SHA256 over S3 objects sufficient? Also we'll include mapping from sampled logs -> full set. @carlos-sre can you start a sampled export and share the query? :thumbsup:

carlos-sre: Starting sample export now. Query we used (Elasticsearch/Kibana):
```
index: "auth-logs-*"
query: {
  "bool": {
    "must": [
      { "term": { "event": "auth.failure" } },
      { "range": { "@timestamp": { "gte": "2026-02-18T00:00:00Z", "lte": "2026-02-19T00:00:00Z" } } }
    ]
  }
}
sort: ["@timestamp:asc"]
size: 5000
```
Export command (will stage to compliance bucket):
```bash
./tools/es-export --index "auth-logs-*" --q-file sample_q.json --out sample_auth_20260218.ndjson
aws s3 cp sample_auth_20260218.ndjson s3://redwood-compliance/pwcevidence/2026-02-18/sample_auth_20260218.ndjson
```
I included deterministic sampling: we used modular sampling by user_id hash (user_id % 100 < 10) to get ~10% sample. Will provide mapping.csv with original doc_ids -> sample_id.

alyssa-oncall: I repro'd the 401 loop in staging with a small script. Steps (short): 1) create test client with canary API key, 2) set header X-Debug-Force-JWT-Expire: 1 (makes token appear expired), 3) disable client-side backoff so it retries immediately, 4) send 400 rps for 3m.
Curl snippet:
```bash
for i in {1..1000}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY" -H "X-Debug-Force-JWT-Expire: 1" https://api.redwood-inference.test/v1/generate >/dev/null &
done
```
This produced the same 401 + refresh loop pattern in staging logs. Warning: do this only in canary/staging.

diane-ctrl: For SOC 2 evidence we require: - retention policy doc (policy id: INF-LOGS-RET-2024) - signed manifest.csv with object paths + sha256s - sampling method description + mapping.csv linking sampled ids to originals - chain-of-custody notes (who exported, when, signed by whom). Ben, confirm TTLs and rotation windows for KMS used to encrypt exports.

ben-security: TL;DR retention/keys: primary auth logs TTL = 90 days (hot), cold archive = 365 days; refresh token TTL = 30 days; session cookie max-age = 14 days. KMS rotation: yearly key rotation for the export key; keystore master rotated 2025-11-01 (next scheduled 2026-11-01). Exports are encrypted with key alias: alias/redwood-compliance-exports. We'll include key manifest + rotation history.

auditor_pwc: Thanks. Two followups: 1) we need the exact export times and the user sampling seed so we can verify randomness; 2) we need a small replay script that reproduces the sequence end-to-end (auth 401 -> repeated refresh attempts -> increased API usage -> billing meter events) so we can validate causal steps.

carlos-sre: Re: replay script — here's a minimal python script that replays the flow against a staging endpoint (uses canary key and debug header). It simulates N clients, each forcing token expiry and retrying refresh, with a short window of sustained requests to trigger meter events.
```python
# replay_auth_spike.py (staging only)
import requests, threading, time
URL = "https://api.redwood-inference.staging/v1/generate"
KEY = "CANARY_KEY"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}", "X-Debug-Force-JWT-Expire": "1"}

def worker(i):
    for _ in range(200):
        r = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={"input":"ping"}, timeout=5)
        # don't backoff to mimic faulty client
        time.sleep(0.05)

threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(i,)) for i in range(20)]
for t in threads: t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()
```
Run with: `python replay_auth_spike.py` (staging only). This produced the 401->refresh burst in my run.

alyssa-oncall: Attaching log excerpt from staging showing the pattern (sanitized):
```
2026-02-18T12:03:12Z auth.failure user=uid:12345 token=expired ip=1.2.3.4 req_id=rA1
2026-02-18T12:03:12Z auth.refresh_attempt user=uid:12345 result=200 req_id=rA2
2026-02-18T12:03:13Z auth.failure user=uid:12345 token=expired req_id=rA3
2026-02-18T12:03:13Z quota.charge meter=token-requests amount=1 user=uid:12345
2026-02-18T12:03:14Z quota.charge meter=token-requests amount=1 user=uid:67890
2026-02-18T12:06:00Z billing.alert spike=high-meter-usage window=3m
```
Mapping: sample doc ids -> originals will be in mapping.csv in export.

ben-security: We'll produce a zipped evidence bundle: `pwcevidence_2026-02-18.zip` containing: - policy_INF-LOGS-RET-2024.pdf - sample_auth_20260218.ndjson - mapping.csv - manifest.csv (path + sha256) - replay_script.py - chain_of_custody.txt - kms_key_manifest.json
We'll upload to s3://redwood-compliance/pwcevidence/2026-02-18/ and share presigned links. ETA EOD Thurs. :white_check_mark:

auditor_pwc: That plan works. One small request: please also include a short README.md inside the bundle that explains the deterministic sampling seed and how to use mapping.csv to reconstruct sample -> full dataset lookups.

ben-security: Will do. Quick question for auditor_pwc: is SHA256 in manifest enough, or do you want a signed HSM attest?

auditor_pwc: SHA256 is sufficient for now. If PwC requests HSM signatures later we'll raise it but not required in initial package.

ben-security: Thanks everyone — we'll post the S3 paths + presigned URLs once the upload completes. If you need the bundle sooner for a deep-dive, DM me and I can share a temporary staging link.

auditor_pwc: Appreciated. Please @mention me when uploads are live. Closing loop on repro: include the replay_script, the sanitized logs excerpt, mapping.csv, and manifest.csv. Thanks all. :pray:
